question: Which hormone causes the muscles in the urinary tract to relax during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles throughout the body, which slows down urine flow and widens the tubes connecting the kidneys to the bladder. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h1)

question: Why is swelling of the kidney (hydronephrosis) more common on the right side during pregnancy?

options.A: The right kidney has a larger baseline vascular supply
options.B: Increased lymphatic drainage on the left abdominal wall
options.C: Left-sided renal agenesis is common in adult females
options.D: Dextrorotation of the uterus and ovarian vein complex compression

explanation: The pregnant womb naturally tilts slightly to the right, putting more pressure on the right ureter and blood vessels. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h1)

question: How does the rate at which the kidneys filter blood (GFR) change during a normal pregnancy?
explanation: Kidneys work harder during pregnancy, filtering waste much faster than usual to clear out both maternal and fetal byproducts. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h2)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks has a serum creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL. What does this indicate?
explanation: Normal creatinine levels drop during pregnancy due to increased filtration, so 0.9 mg/dL is actually higher than expected and points to possible kidney strain. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h2)

question: How do the kidneys help balance the mild breathing-related alkalosis common in pregnant women?

options.A: Absorbing more carbon dioxide through skin
options.B: Retaining excess hydrogen ions in the blood
options.C: Excreting more bicarbonate in the urine

explanation: The kidneys pass out more bicarbonate in the urine to balance the changes in blood pH caused by faster breathing. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h3)

question: What is the main reason a pregnant woman's body holds onto more sodium?

options.C: Direct stimulation by human growth hormone

explanation: The body retains sodium to hold onto the extra water needed to build up blood volume and body fluids for the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h3)

question: What happens to blood flow through the kidneys at the peak of a contraction during labor?
explanation: Strong contractions temporarily reduce blood flow to both the uterus and the kidneys for a short moment. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h4)

question: Why is having a very full bladder dangerous during the active phase of labor?

options.B: It causes immediate permanent kidney failure
options.C: It can obstruct fetal descent and weaken contractions
options.D: It stops the production of amniotic fluid

explanation: A full bladder takes up valuable space in the pelvis, which can slow down the baby's movement downward. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h4)

question: What is a normal urinary pattern within the first 48 hours after giving birth?
explanation: The sudden drop in pregnancy hormones causes the body to produce large amounts of urine to get rid of extra pregnancy fluids. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h5)

question: Why are women more prone to urinary tract infections right after delivery?

options.B: Complete loss of normal microflora in the kidneys
options.C: Sudden permanent damage to the renal glomeruli
options.D: Bladder hypoesthesia and residual urine stasis

explanation: Reduced bladder feeling after birth means the bladder might not empty completely, leaving pooled urine where bacteria can easily grow. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h5)

question: A patient six hours after delivery has not urinated, and her bladder feels full above the pubic bone. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Assist the patient to the toilet and encourage voiding
options.B: Administer a potent intravenous loop diuretic
options.C: Wait another six hours for spontaneous micturition
options.D: Document normal findings and restrict fluid intake

explanation: Helping the patient to the bathroom to try urinating naturally is always the first step before trying invasive methods like catheters. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h6)

question: Which sign is most important to watch for when checking a pregnant woman for early kidney issues related to preeclampsia?

options.A: New-onset persistent proteinuria and rising blood pressure
options.B: Decreased maternal heart rate and low body temperature
options.C: Increased production of clear, dilute amniotic fluid
options.D: Drastic drop in serum uric acid levels below baseline

explanation: Preeclampsia affects the kidney filters, which shows up clinically as high blood pressure combined with protein spilling into the urine. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h6)
